title: The Barrens
body: The Barrens is a vast savanna of red earth and thorny scrub in the heart of Kalimdor, between the forests of Ashenvale and the canyons of Thousand Needles. Long ago it was night elf woodland, until war and the Sundering scorched it dry. In recent years new oases have formed, fed by some power seeping up from below. The Horde holds the Crossroads where the great roads meet, while centaurs, quilboar and harpies contest the land, goblins run the port of Ratchet and Theramore's soldiers hold Northwatch on the coast.

title: The Crossroads
body: The Crossroads is the largest Horde town in the Barrens, a walled outpost raised where its great roads cross. Thork leads its defenses in the Warchief's name and the shaman Sergra Darkthorn sets newcomers to work, and Razormane raids on the caravans from Durotar keep the garrison busy. From dawn till dusk the warrior Mankrik watches the horizon, grieving the wife he lost fighting the quilboar.

parts.body: Mankrik's wife was found at last in the south, beaten and left where she fell, clearly dead in battle. When the news reached him he asked nothing more.

title: Dreadmist Peak
body: Dreadmist Peak rises from the plains north of the Crossroads, and cultists of the Burning Blade have made it their own. In a cave near the summit, the Dreadmist Den, the Demon Seed rests above an altar of demonic fire: the object of power around which the cult rallies, and a tool of the Burning Legion itself.

parts.body: A flawed power stone set at the altar destroyed the Demon Seed. Its destruction sent waves through the ether, and others, it is feared, felt them and will wonder who broke their toy.

title: The Mor'shan Rampart
body: In the far north of the Barrens, where the grass gives way to the forests of Ashenvale, the Horde has raised the Mor'shan Rampart, a fortified wall and watch tower to hold the border against the night elves. From it Kadrak leads the Horde's campaign in Ashenvale, sending recruits on to the outposts at Splintertree and the Zoram Strand.

title: Ratchet
body: Ratchet is the goblin port on the Barrens coast, founded by Gazlowe, Thrall's chief engineer, with the gold the Warchief paid him for building Orgrimmar. A town of the Steamwheedle Cartel, it is open to all who trade in peace, and its boat carries cargo across the sea to Booty Bay. Business would be perfect but for the Southsea Freebooters, who camp almost on Gazlowe's doorstep along the Merchant Coast and raid his ships.

title: Northwatch Hold
body: Northwatch Hold is a human fortress on the coast south of Ratchet, held by marines of Theramore and blocking the coastal road toward Dustwallow Marsh. Captain Fairmount commands it, and her cannoneers have sunk so many ships that Ratchet's privateers call them trigger happy louts. Offshore lurks Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, a sea beast the humans have every reason to fear.

title: The Oases of the Barrens
body: In recent years green oases have sprung up across the Barrens, the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater and the Stagnant Oasis, and the druid Tonga Runetotem of the Crossroads senses a power leaking up through them. Kolkar centaurs camp beside all three. Beneath the Lushwater opens the mouth of the Wailing Caverns, where the druid Naralex went down hoping to dream the Barrens green again, and his dream turned to nightmare.

parts.body: Deep beneath the Forgotten Pools lies a fissure in the earth with gases bubbling up from it, perhaps the source of the life now stirring in the Barrens.

title: Camp Taurajo
body: Camp Taurajo is the tauren outpost of the southern Barrens, on the road east from Mulgore where young tauren first come down from their homeland, for the lives of the tauren and the orcs are now intertwined. The hunter Jorn Skyseer teaches that this land teems with life for one who knows where to look, and the camp's strangest resident is a caged Razormane, Mangletooth, who has information to sell.

title: Field of Giants
body: South of Camp Taurajo spreads the Field of Giants, where great mounds of earth rise from the grass. Silithid have made their hives here, insects new to the Barrens, and those who watch them are uneasy: they show more wit than any beast should, and reports of them have reached Orgrimmar.

parts.body: Jorn Skyseer could read nothing of the great harvester's nature, for its spirit had fled, but he fears the silithid herald a grim future for his people.

title: Bael Modan
body: South of the Field of Giants the dwarves of Ironforge have torn open the earth at Bael Modan, blasting deep holes with explosives and machines under the guard of Bael'dun Keep. The land was not empty: tauren of the Stonespire tribe lived here, and many were killed or driven off when the dwarves came. Gann Stonespire, who tried and failed to find a peaceful end, now walks the Gold Road seeking revenge.

parts.body: With the dwarves' own explosives Gann had their flying machine blown apart, an insult to the memory of his tribe repaid.

title: The Razorfen
body: In the far south of the Barrens, near the Thousand Needles, rise the Razorfen, the greatest of all the thorn clusters. The quilboar hold that they are the very body of their boar god Agamaggan, who fell in the War of the Ancients, and that the entrance to the Razorfen Downs is his great maw. In Razorfen Kraul the crone Charlga Razorflank musters a foul army.
